va_harkening_hill.blurb: Harkening Hill is a pure bouldering hillside in Southwest Virginia, reached from the Blue Ridge Parkway within roughly an hour of Roanoke, Blacksburg or Lynchburg. Hundreds of gneiss blocks, roughly 5 to 30 feet tall, are scattered over a slope that faces south and west, with a few wide gullies between them. Problems run from V0 to V8, centered on the V2 to V5 range, with subtle crimps, slopers and poor footholds rather than big jugs. The Stones holds well over half of the problems, with Inner Circle and Upper Deck next. The tall lines there are praised for mostly excellent landings. Fall, winter and early spring suit it best; summer brings heat and thick foliage. Expect ticks and poison ivy away from the worn paths.

ca_north_wonderland_approach.blurb: North Wonderland Approach is the southern gateway to the northern Wonderland of Rocks in Joshua Tree National Park. Trad climbing dominates, with a fair number of top-rope laps, some bolted lines and a handful of boulder problems. Grades are mostly moderate to mid-range, with a scattering of easy climbs and a few hard ones at the top. The terrain is domes, slabs, dihedrals and cracks spread over many small formations, among them Reggie Dome, Outward Bound Slab, Cool Dome, Hidden Dome and Gilligan's Island. The walk in is flat but long, often over an hour each way, which keeps the area far quieter than the park's roadside crags. It suits climbers who like finding obscure lines and having a dome to themselves.

mt_big_sky_area.blurb: Big Sky Area covers the Gallatin Canyon corridor south of Bozeman, with crags on both sides of the river along Highway 191 and side drainages that climb into the Gallatin Range. Bouldering makes up most of the climbing, from the high-elevation gneiss blocks at Hidden Lakes to the scattered boulders around Greek Creek, mostly V0 to V4 with a tail up to V7. Sport routes, mainly 5.9 to 5.12, gather around Red Cliff, while Beehive Basin and the Sphinx and Helmet area hold alpine, ice and mixed lines. Rock quality varies and is not as solid as at other Montana destinations. Many crags here are lightly developed, so expect some exploring.

qc_parc_de_la_falaise_cach_e.blurb: This climbing park sits in Saint-Alphonse-Rodriguez, in the Lanaudière region of Quebec. Its main cliff, Chez Roger, is a gneiss wall about 500 metres long and 20 to 60 metres high, made of thin horizontal bands with a rough, abrasive texture. It faces southeast, so it gets plenty of sun, while the deciduous forest at its base gives shade in summer. Sport and trad routes are about equally common, on steep crimpy faces, overhanging arêtes and hand cracks. Sport climbs mostly fall between 5.10 and 5.12, with a smaller group of moderates, and the trad lines lean toward beginners. A separate boulder sector holds about three dozen problems, mostly below V5, and was developed only in recent years, so some holds may be brittle.

az_christopher_creek_gorge.blurb: Christopher Creek Gorge is a riparian canyon in central Arizona, near 5,000 feet, whose creek runs on toward Tonto Creek and Roosevelt Lake. Most visitors come for canyoneering, yet the walls carry a good number of routes, with sport making up about two thirds and the rest trad. Grades run from 5.7 to 5.12, with the bulk between 5.9 and 5.11. The Southern Wall is clean quartzite that stays shaded all day. Other groupings include Spring Creek, Waterfall Area, Confluence Wall and Eden. The canyon's north side takes sun and works well in winter, while the shaded south side is more comfortable when it is warm. July and August are best skipped for heat and insects.
